title: 2026: 15th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Radboud University
Nijmegen
 When
12–13 March 2026
 Where
Elinor Ostromgebouw, Heyendaalseweg 141, 6525 AJ Nijmegen






 Download the programme





2 days 10 papers Roundtable Radboud Special


Radboud University hosted the fifteenth edition in the Elinor Ostromgebouw — a building named for the economist of the commons. After an official opening by Saskia Lavrijssen, ten papers ran from a choice framework for empirical research design and hiring women in Bangladesh to firms facing uncertainty in Uganda, social capital and gender equality, newborn health during Covid-19, structural change in India, colonial institutional transfer, affirmative action and inequality in climate preferences.
Two additions broadened the programme: a Radboud Special on heritage diets by Quirijn de Mast of Radboudumc, and a roundtable on the research needs of development practice, with IPA, SNV, HKV, FMO, CARE and IOB. It was also the first workshop with Erasmus University Rotterdam among the co-organizing universities, bringing the network to eight.
The local organizer was Natascha Wagner. The workshop was jointly organized and co-sponsored by the network and its participating universities, represented by their node coordinators: Arjun Bedi (Erasmus), Mark Treurniet (Groningen), Natascha Wagner (Radboud), Patricio Dalton (Tilburg), Eleonora Nillesen (UNU-MERIT), Karlijn Morsink (Utrecht), Marc Witte (Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam) and Francesco Cecchi (Wageningen).

Jonas Gathen, Tilburg University Inequality and the Dynamics of Growth: Evidence from 25 Years of Structural Change in India Discussant: Peter Lanjouw, VU Amsterdam
Radboud Special Quirijn de Mast, Radboudumc Heritage Diets



Friday 13 March

title: 2025: 14th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Tinbergen Institute
Graduate School and Research Institute for Economics and Business
 When
27–28 March 2025
 Where
Gustav Mahlerplein 117, 1082 MS Amsterdam






 Download the programme





2 days 9 papers Invited talk 6 posters


The 14th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop was hosted by the Tinbergen Institute, in Amsterdam. Chaired by Marc Witte, the event took place on 27 and 28 March 2025 and included various academic and social activities, among which paper presentations, social lunches and dinner, and poster presentations. For a detailed version of the full itinerary, please download the workshop program.
Nine papers ranged from education after a natural disaster and protectionist FDI rules in Indonesia to legal trade and drug trafficking, mental accounting and cash transfers, youth mental health, drought insurance, how far to trust observational estimates, colonial legacies and fertility, and tax nudges among firms in Kampala. Jonathan Morduch of New York University spoke on selecting experimental sites for external validity, and six researchers presented posters.
The workshop was jointly organized and co-sponsored by the network, the Tinbergen Institute and the participating universities of Groningen, Radboud, Tilburg, UNU-MERIT, Utrecht, the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and Wageningen.


Programme

Clotilde Mahé, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Cash Transfers and Youth Mental Health: Improving Behaviour but Feeling No Better Discussant: Laura Metzger, Radboud University Nijmegen



Friday 28 March

Harry Hyuk Son, Utrecht University Tailoring Advice and Incentives to Enhance Consumer Welfare from Catastrophic Drought Insurance Discussant: Ashley Wong, Tilburg University
Jon de Quidt, Queen Mary University of London How Much Should We Trust Observational Estimates? Accumulating Evidence Using Randomized Controlled Trials with Imperfect Compliance Discussant: Marc Witte, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam & Tinbergen Institute

title: 2024: 13th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Utrecht University
 When
18–19 April 2024
 Where
Janskerkhof 2-3, 3512 BK Utrecht






 Download the programme





2 days 11 papers


Utrecht University hosted the thirteenth edition at Janskerkhof, in the heart of the city. Eleven papers from Warwick, the Stockholm School of Economics, Bocconi, the University of Ghana and across the network took up job loss and job search, mobile internet and structural change in Nigeria, seed markets, incentives in a community health programme in Sierra Leone, culture and competition, female entrepreneurship, early-childhood skills in Roma communities in Bulgaria, temperature and manufacturing in India, mobile salary payments in Afghanistan and child stunting.
The local organizing team was Patricio Dalton and Harry Son. The workshop was jointly organized and co-sponsored by the network and its participating universities, represented by their node coordinators: Wendy Janssens (Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam), Karlijn Morsink (Utrecht), Patricio Dalton (Tilburg), Kristina Czura (Groningen), Natascha Wagner (Nijmegen), Eleonora Nillesen (UNU-MERIT) and Francesco Cecchi (Wageningen).

title: 2023: 12th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
University of Groningen
 When
20–21 April 2023
 Where
Doopsgezinde Kerk, Oude Boteringestraat 33, 9712 GD Groningen






 Download the programme





2 days 12 papers


The twelfth edition met in the Kerkzaal of the Doopsgezinde Kerk, in the centre of Groningen. Its programme names the network itself as co-organizer, alongside seven participating universities, and it switched to a tighter format than earlier editions: 45 minutes per paper — 30 to present, 5 for the discussant and 10 for discussion.
Twelve papers brought speakers from the World Bank, LSE, MIT Sloan, Nova School of Business and Economics and Universitat Pompeu Fabra together with researchers from across the Dutch universities. They covered crop insurance, slum upgrading in the Dominican Republic, the political legacies of trade liberalization in Brazil, land markets in Uganda and Kenya, menstrual health at work, child marriage, aspirations, e-money, jobs and political participation in Ethiopia, universal basic income in Kenya, evidence use among civil servants in Pakistan and trust in public services.
The local organizing team was Kristina Czura, Robert Lensink and Kritika Saxena. The workshop was jointly organized and co-sponsored by the network and the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Utrecht University, Tilburg University, the University of Groningen, Nijmegen University, UNU-MERIT and Wageningen University.


Programme

title: 2022: 11th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Maastricht University
at UNU-MERIT
 When
21–22 April 2022
 Where
UNU-MERIT, Boschstraat 24, 6211 AX Maastricht






 Download the programme





2 days 10 papers


The first workshop since 2019 met at UNU-MERIT in Maastricht, with Maastricht University joining the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Tilburg and Wageningen as co-organizers. Ten papers over two days put public services and accountability centre stage — free riding in service delivery in India, community service providers in Sierra Leone, social accountability for teachers, community-based monitoring — alongside climate-smart agriculture, seasonal migration loans, menstrual health and schooling in Bangladesh, texting parents about early child development, female admission caps in Iran and the history of pro-birth policies in Congo.
The organizing team was Eleonora Nillesen, Yannick Markhof and Karthika Sujatha, together with Erwin Bulte, Patricio S. Dalton, Wendy Janssens, Menno Pradhan and Maarten Voors. The workshop was co-sponsored by the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (School of Business and Economics), Tilburg University (Department of Economics) and Wageningen University (Development Economics Group), with external funding from the Stichting Universiteitsfonds Limburg (SWOL).

title: 2018: 9th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Wageningen University
Development Economics Group
 When
18 April 2018
 Where
Impulse, Stippeneng 2, 6708 Wageningen






 Download the programme





1 day 6 papers


The ninth edition was a focused one-day workshop in Impulse, on the Wageningen campus. Six papers — each with its own discussant — took on goals and support groups for microentrepreneurs in Medellín, the origins of violence in Rwanda, barriers to female empowerment in Tanzania, the political economy of school test scores, land markets and agricultural productivity, and how small-scale retailers learn business practices from their peers.
The workshop was co-sponsored by Tilburg University (Department of Economics) and Wageningen University (Development Economics Group and Wageningen School of Social Sciences).

title: 2016: 7th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Tilburg University
Department of Economics
 When
10–11 March 2016
 Where
Cobbenhagen building, Warandelaan 2, 5037 AB Tilburg






 Download the programme





2 days 9 papers 3 early-research talks


Back in Tilburg for its seventh edition, the workshop gained a new partner in the University of Lucerne. Finance ran through much of the programme — joint-liability lending against rainwater tanks in Kenya, sharing borrower information, relationship banking and informal debt in China — alongside teacher pay in Indonesia, informal taxation on the Congo river, the roots of conflict and an overpaid public sector.
The DFID early-research session returned with new work on skilled labour and finance among SMEs in Uganda, mobile money adoption in Kenya, and poverty and cognitive function among small retailers in Vietnam.
The organizing team was Thorsten Beck, Erwin Bulte, Patricio S. Dalton, Manuel Oechslin and Burak Uras. The workshop was co-sponsored by Tilburg University, Wageningen University, the University of Lucerne and the DFID research programme on innovation and growth in low-income countries.

title: 2013: 4th Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Tilburg University
with Wageningen University
 When
13–14 June 2013
 Where
Dante and Koopmans buildings, Warandelaan 2, 5037 AB Tilburg






 Download the programme





2 days 8 papers PhD session


The fourth edition returned to Tilburg University, now organized jointly by Tilburg and Wageningen — a partnership that carried the workshop through the years that followed. Over two days in the Dante and Koopmans buildings, eight papers covered market access and internal migration, tariff evasion, financial development, eye disease, resource windfalls, the long shadow of the slave trade, free education in Cambodia and unemployment benefits.
The programme also included a session for PhD students, with three shorter presentations from Tilburg and Wageningen. Among the presenters was Francesco Cecchi, who would later serve as the network’s coordinator at Wageningen.
The workshop was organized by Thorsten Beck, Erwin Bulte, Benedikt Goderis and Manuel Oechslin, and sponsored by Tilburg University (Department of Economics and CentER) and Wageningen University.

title: 2010: 1st Dutch Development Economics Network Workshop
text:
Tilburg University
Department of Economics

 Where
Dante building, Warandelaan 2, 5037 AB Tilburg






 Download the programme





2 days 7 papers Tilburg


Where it all started. The first edition — then simply called the Development Economics Workshop — brought researchers from Tilburg, Wageningen and VU Amsterdam together with guests from Bocconi, Stockholm, Warwick, Göttingen, Lausanne, Bonn and the University of Amsterdam for two days in the Dante building at Tilburg University.
The discussant format that still anchors the workshop was there from the start: each paper had 60 minutes — 40 for the presentation, 10 for an assigned discussant and 10 for general discussion. The programme ranged from relational contracts in Kenya’s flower exports and group lending in Chiapas to bank ownership, contract enforcement and the costs of politically motivated aid, with an open discussion moderated by Thorsten Beck.
The workshop was organized by Thorsten Beck and Manuel Oechslin, and sponsored by CentER, the Tilburg School of Economics and Management and the university’s Economics Department.

text:
Wageningen University
Development Economics Group

Leeuwenborch building, Hollandseweg 1, 6706 KN Wageningen






 Download the programme





2 days 9 papers 3 early-research talks


The sixth edition moved to Wageningen University, with every session held in room C76 of the Leeuwenborch building. Nine papers spanned national capabilities and competitiveness, civil unrest, weather forecasting in semi-arid India, investment liberalisation in China, how interview modes change measured village networks, malaria insurance in Nigeria, business training in Vietnam, vulnerability lines and redistribution preferences.
Alongside them ran a session of early results from the DFID research programme Coordinated Country Case Studies – Innovation and Growth: Raising Productivity in Low Income Countries, with three shorter talks on mobile money, retailers in Jakarta and exporters in South Africa.
The workshop was co-sponsored by Tilburg University (Department of Economics), Wageningen University (Development Economics Group) and the DFID research programme.

For its tenth edition the workshop came to Amsterdam, hosted at the Tinbergen Institute, with the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam joining Tilburg and Wageningen as co-sponsor. Nine papers covered aid fragmentation and conflict, mobile-phone monitoring in Niger, free university tuition in Ecuador, health care during Sierra Leone’s Ebola outbreak, payment technology, community natural-resource management in Namibia, crop insurance bundles in Kenya, management consulting in Colombia and schooling for displaced children in Jordan.
The workshop closed with Peter Lanjouw on How Lives Change: Palanpur, India, and Development Economics, drawn from the long-running study of a single village in north India. That same afternoon, Jenny Aker also presented at the Tinbergen Institute’s labor seminar series.
The workshop was co-sponsored by the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (School of Business and Economics), the Tinbergen Institute, Tilburg University (Department of Economics) and Wageningen University (Development Economics Group).

title: 2023: 1st Dutch Development Economics Network PhD Workshop
text:
Utrecht University
 When
10 November 2023
 Where
Utrecht University, Utrecht






 Download the programme





1 day 14 PhD presentations 7 universities


The network’s first workshop dedicated to PhD students gave the floor entirely to early-career researchers. Fourteen PhD candidates — two from each of the seven participating universities in Amsterdam, Groningen, Maastricht, Nijmegen, Tilburg, Utrecht and Wageningen — presented their work in 25-minute slots over a single day at Utrecht University, and the day ended with dinner.
Child marriage and intimate partner violence, vulnerability within institutions, attitudes towards refugees, pensions and old-age support, crop insurance, parental migration, soft skills in school, Covid-19 and economic mobility, foreign aid, seed access and nutrition, social media and gender norms, and the aftermath of war were among the topics.

Forum, Droevendaalsesteeg 2, Wageningen (day 1) · Leeuwenborch, Hollandseweg 1 (day 2)






 Download the programme





2 days 7 papers 7 posters Skills sessions


Wageningen University hosted the second PhD workshop over two days. On the first, in the Forum building, seven PhD candidates presented full papers and seven more presented posters, in sessions chaired by Yannick Markhof and Elisa van Dongen. Research ranged from crop insurance and welfare under catastrophic drought to anti-poverty transfers and self-belief, 3G coverage and child marriage, child care subsidies in Egypt, mineral trade and armed conflict in eastern Congo, and a refugee camp’s effect on its hosts.
The second day, in the Leeuwenborch, turned to the craft of research: Wageningen faculty ran two rounds of parallel sessions on preparing for the academic job market, the publication process and writing a response letter, moving from a research idea to an empirical strategy and a story, machine learning in economics, research designs with observational data, building a CV and writing a research proposal.

title: 2025: 3rd Dutch Development Economics Network PhD Workshop
text:
Tinbergen Institute
Amsterdam
 When
31 October 2025
 Where
Gustav Mahlerplein 117, 1082 MS Amsterdam






 Download the programme





1 day 8 papers 8 posters


The third PhD workshop filled a day at the Tinbergen Institute in Amsterdam. Eight PhD candidates presented papers, each paired with a discussant from across the network, and eight more pitched their work in a rapid-fire poster session — seven minutes per poster, with a bell announcing each new round.
Research ranged from Mexico’s penal justice reform and intimate partner violence in India to aspirations and child outcomes, eldercare, the dynamics of discrimination, insurance decisions within the household, elites and human capital in Peru, and gendered climate policy. Sessions were chaired by Davide Manzoni, Juan Segnana, Anne Lieke Ebbers and Nicola Mangraviti — Anne Lieke Ebbers having presented at the first PhD workshop in 2023. The day closed with dinner at the Tinbergen Institute.
